The existing observed endpoints are 1 (17 rows) and 10 (7 rows); changed data would span 2–11 with seven scores of 11, breaching the documented maximum by exactly one; the ten-unit-wide observed scale is displaced one step above the documented 1–10 interval, yielding original A=stored-1.

33.description: Charge terms for a return that no rule of the schedule matches.
33.definition: A return that matches no rule of the Return Handling Charge Schedule takes the Standard Handling Charge: flat_charge 15.00 and charge_pct 5.0.

34.definition: $$RHC = F + \frac{P}{100} \times V$$ where F is flat_charge and P is charge_pct of a rule of the schedule that matches the return (or of the Standard Handling Charge), and V is products.unit_value of the returned item, in the currency units of unit_value. Every row of returns has an RHC. A customer's or group's RHC over a period is the sum over its returns whose revdate falls in the period; its average is that sum divided by the number of those returns. No intermediate rounding; round only the reported result, to 2 decimals.

doc_edits.new: a criterion that places no restriction matches every return, one whose value is missing included, and any other criterion never matches a return whose value is NULL (for example a customer whose seg_category is NULL).

g2.data_shows: [56] explicitly says availability_pct is a percentage on a 0-to-100 scale; [8] says 99% is typical availability. Existing values span 95.00–99.99, hence changed values span 0.9500–0.9999, including PV937101: 97.73 -> 0.9773; PV945724: 96.91 -> 0.9691. These values are fractional availability, so multiply by exactly 100 to obtain the documented percent.
